label: COUNTS-ONLY amendment (2026-10-31): native hashed ECDLP bounded end-to-end feasibility, four prime rosters (counted S only, no wall time)
description: Supersedes, for counted S only, research/hashed_ecdl_ecbench_20261030/spec.json at 3ae1ac2bd (copied unchanged to research/hashed_ecdl_counts_20261031/frozen-source/). Same nine arms and every arm parameter, same roster 10/12/14/16, same public targets (target_seed 2026103001, 8 per curve), same seed 2026103002, order shuffle and 30 s per-execution budget. Only measurement changes. Gate-forced change: isolation_required L2 to L0. On EKS the run-ecbench L2 gate grades any solve under 1 ms as L1 (record.rs MIN_SOLVE_WALL_NS_V3) and exits 42, and rho at 10-16 bits solves in microseconds (run gh-41008826427-1: 176/192 records L1); L0 is the level ecbench documents as sufficient for operation counts. Discretionary changes, filed before any data (protocol v2): rounds 5 to 1 (S is a deterministic function of (workload, algorithm seed) and replays exactly; more rounds would add walk seeds per target, i.e. power, which the expected H2 effect does not need) and warmup 1 to 0 (a warm-up only absorbs one-time wall costs, which counted S does not see; the measured round then uses absolute seed index 0, which no measured round of the original used). The binary must be built from commit 3ae1ac2bd63d3fb0e86b7e8c0af2b5ec0f1bd09d: ic.hashed_native_v1 is not on main. All cold stages and unknown/exhausted outcomes are retained. Native S is a lower bound (native arithmetic is not completely priced). The 30 s timeout_seconds is a wall-clock limit (runner.rs): at L0 whether a native row ends verified or timeout depends on the host, so the set of complete (backend, curve) cells depends on the host; a timeout row is host censoring (unknown), never a negative result. No wall-time figure from this session is a result. Caveat: on 64-bit builds lambda <= 64, root_u = lambda/131072 = 0 and public inputs take the finite-size fallback; nothing here exercises the recursive subexponential kernel; ic.tensor_contraction_v1 is an exponential toy (protocol H1). Protocol: research/hashed_ecdl_counts_20261031/protocol.json (v2).
